categories.name: Create and dispatch a feature or bug task to a free birocode agent
categories.description: The most common request: a described feature or bug for the harness, turned into a card and dispatched to a free birocode repo agent — end to end, a descriptive PR with screenshots, no merge, no deploy.
categories.template: Another task for a free birocode agent: <what and why, in a few sentences>. Work end to end on a feature branch and open a descriptive PR with screenshots. Do not merge, do not deploy.
categories.tip: Describe the behaviour you want, name the tab or screen; say "free agent" (or name one), "PR with screenshots", and "no merge / no deploy".

categories.name: Nudge / follow-up on the previous request
categories.description: Short follow-ups that keep the arch moving: continue, so?, is it done yet, go ahead, do both. They carry no new request — the arch picks up where it left off.
categories.template: Continue from where you left off. / So, is it done? Ping it again. / Go ahead with both.
categories.tip: When the arch stalls, a short nudge works; for a changed plan, restate the task instead.

examples.text: so come on did you do it or what?`

categories.name: Pull main and redeploy this hub
categories.description: A merged PR should go live on the hub (DESKTOP-POAPPP3) only: the arch sends the hub's birocode agent the guarded self-deploy order and reports the build and the health check.
categories.template: We merged PR #<n> in birocode. Pull main and redeploy the harness on this computer only; report the commit and whether it restarted healthy.
categories.tip: Say "this computer / our hub only" — otherwise it is read as a fleet update.

categories.name: PR follow-up: resolve merge conflicts, post the missing PR, finish up
categories.description: A PR has conflicts or an agent finished without posting one: the arch orders the responsible agent to resolve, rebase and repost, or to publish its PR.
categories.template: PR #<n> has merge conflicts — tell the responsible agent to resolve them and repost the PR. (Or: agent X finished but posted no PR — order it to push its branch and open one.)
categories.tip: Give the PR number or the task id; say if a free agent may take it over when the original one is unknown.

categories.name: Update the whole fleet (or named machines) to the newest build
categories.description: After merges to main: every harness in the fleet — or a named subset, with exceptions — pulls main and redeploys itself. The arch sends each machine's birocode agent the redeploy order or upgrades the peer directly.
categories.template: We merged new PRs in birocode. Update all fleet harnesses to the newest main (except <machine>, it is busy) — each pulls main and redeploys; report which build each one is on.
categories.tip: Name the exceptions (busy machines) and whether a dirty main may be cleared; say "everywhere" or list the machines.

categories.name: Report a dashboard / harness bug (becomes a bug card for the right machine)
categories.description: A thing on the management dashboard or in a harness does not work — the arch confirms where it fails and files a bug card for the agent of the machine that owns the code (usually the hub's birocode agent).
categories.template: Bug: on the management dashboard, <what you did> does nothing / shows <wrong thing> (machine <x>, agent <y>). Find the cause and fix it — a PR with the root cause and screenshots, no merge, no deploy.
categories.tip: Say what you clicked, where, and what you expected; name the machine the bug is visible on.

categories.name: Fulfil an approved repo-agent request (goal conversation)
categories.description: A repo agent asked the arch for something (files, a peer's help, a decision). Once the Operator approves it on the Repo Agent Requests tab, the arch fulfils it — usually in a goal conversation that drives the peers until done.
categories.template: (Approve the request on the Repo Agent Requests tab, then:) Fulfil the approved request from <machine>/<repo>: <what it asked>. Drive the involved agents until it is done and report.
categories.tip: Approve first; the arch then starts a goal conversation. Say "the loop capped but you are not finished" to continue one.

categories.name: Reflect reality on a card: merged / done / move it to the right column
categories.description: A task is already merged or finished (or handed to someone else) but its card lags: the arch verifies and moves the card, or marks it done on the Operator's word.
categories.template: We merged task <id> / PR #<n> — reflect that on the card (move it to Done). (Or: check whether task <id> is finished and merged, then move it where it belongs.)
categories.tip: Paste the task id (or the PR number); say "done even if not finished" when you just want it off your plate.

categories.name: Investigate what happened on an agent or a PR
categories.description: Something looks off — an agent went quiet, merged to main directly, a card lies, a link does not work: the arch reads transcripts, git state and the board and explains.
categories.template: On <machine> check the <repo> agent: what did it do, is it finished, did it post a PR? / Why is task <id> still in progress — is that true?
categories.tip: Name the machine and the repo agent (or the task id); ask for the evidence, not a guess.

categories.name: Explain a harness concept or a tool
categories.description: What are goal conversations, what is the Committed column, can you create recurring tasks, do you see the ideas — the arch explains from the harness docs and its tools.
categories.template: What are goal conversations and how do they differ from the arch conversation? / What is the <column> column in the Kanban supposed to be? / Are you able to <do X>?
categories.tip: Ask one concept at a time; follow up with "then do it" to turn the answer into work.

categories.name: Create a tracking-only card (do not ping the agent)
categories.description: A card on the Kanban for work an agent is already doing by itself, so it can be followed on the board. The arch creates the card and sends nothing.
categories.template: Make a card for <machine>'s <repo> agent — it is already working on <what>. Do not contact the agent, we just want to track it on the board.
categories.tip: Say "do not contact / do not delegate" explicitly, name the machine and the repo agent.

categories.name: Reassign or re-send a card to another agent / machine
categories.description: Work moved between machines or was dispatched to the wrong agent: the arch changes the assignee and, when asked, sends the task again.

categories.name: Tell the arch about scope, access or credentials you changed

categories.name: Order an agent to reset its repo: abandon work, clean, back to main

categories.tip: Say explicitly that uncommitted work may be dropped; otherwise the arch asks the agent to commit first.
